stem.en: Viruses contain genetic material but lack cellular organisation. Which statement explains why they fit none of the five kingdoms?

text.en: They have a nucleus, but it is too small for the kingdom tests to find.

feedback.en: A virus has no nucleus, because it has no cell at all.

text.en: They belong in Monera really, as they are small and have no nucleus.

feedback.en: Monera holds cells without a nucleus. A virus is not a cell.

text.en: Every kingdom holds organisms made of cells, and a virus has no cell.

feedback.en: Right. The system sorts cells, so a virus cannot enter it. This shows a limit of the system.

text.en: They make their own food in a way that no kingdom test can describe.

feedback.en: A virus makes no food. It stays inactive outside a host cell.

explanation.en: A virus has genetic material but no cell, and it stays inactive outside a host cell. Every kingdom is a group of organisms made of cells, so the first test cannot be applied.

hints.en: What does the first test in the five kingdom system ask about?
